packet.headline_seed: Group planned to attack White House UFC event using snipers and drones, FBI says
packet.description_seed: In newly unsealed court filings, the government says the group allegedly expressed grievances about corruption, the Epstein files, and data centres.

what: Group planned to attack White House UFC event using snipers and drones, FBI says

clean_source_blocks.text: In newly unsealed court filings, the government says the group allegedly expressed grievances about corruption, the Epstein files, and data centres.

His mother called local authorities late in the evening on 10 June - just days before the high-profile event - because she was concerned about his large firearms purchases and what she had seen of his online communication with a group that claimed to be made up of former military members and Christian-based. The group allegedly wanted to "jumpstart" a revolution by shooting at "high-value targets" - identified as wealthy people and politicians - attending the fight, and had specifically discussed "grievances about government corruption, the handling of the Epstein files, data centers taking up all the water in communities, and other government actions", according to court documents.

By using the drones, the plotters aimed to spark panic and draw the fleeing crowd toward a sniper team, according to the court documents.. A "second wave" of attackers then allegedly was supposed to storm the White House gate. An estimated 4,300 people were present for the invite-only event on the South Lawn - and another 85,000 were able to watch at a nearby fan zone - as 14 mixed martial arts fighters competed in back-to-back fights on Sunday, The plot was discovered through Tycen Proper, a 19-year-old Ohio man, who was communicating with a group online who "expressed ultra-religious and antigovernment sentiments," federal prosecutors said in the unsealed charges.

The FBI thwarted a plot targeting Sunday's UFC event at the White House, and has taken multiple suspects into custody, according to the agency's head, Kash Patel. Part of the plan involved striking nearby buildings with explosive-laden drones, according to court documents unsealed on Tuesday. One suspect was arrested in Ohio last week, where investigators obtained access to encrypted messages involving other alleged plotters. He has been charged with conspiracy to commit an offence against the US and attempted murder of a federal officer, according to the documents. "Allegedly planned attacks were stopped cold," Patel said in a social media post on Tuesday about the "multi-state operation". Five people are in custody, CBS News, the BBC's US news partner, reported. The BBC has requested further comment from the FBI.

[Lähde: The Guardian]
Multiple arrests made in ‘multi-state operation’ to disrupt alleged drone and gun plot targeting Trump birthday

Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

Law enforcement officials disrupted an attempt to attack the UFC cage fighting event staged at the White House on Sunday with guns and explosive-laden drones, and multiple people were in custody, federal US authorities said.

Five people were arrested from states including Ohio, Missouri and California, said a law enforcement official familiar with the matter. The official spoke to the Associated Press on the condition of anonymity to discuss information that was not yet public.

Federal court records in Cincinnati, Ohio, that were reviewed by the Guardian identify one of the arrested suspects as Tycen Proper, 19. Proper’s mother called the police on 10 June to report concerns about her son’s behavior, his purchase of firearms, and communications with individuals online, those court records said.

According to a federal criminal complaint filed against him, Proper said he had been in contact with individuals online since March. His mother said they claimed to be ex-military and Christian-based.

Local police then had Proper admitted to a hospital for homicidal ideation, and they contacted the FBI. In an interview with a case worker who was present, Proper told authorities that members of the group online believed the US was headed in the wrong direction. Proper also said that some did not want people involved with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein – a former friend of Donald Trump – running the country.

Proper allegedly said he and others planned to first hold a demonstration outside the White House on Sunday as it hosted a mixed-martial arts extravaganza on the South Lawn. As that took place, the group would remotely fly drones “laden with unspecified explosives” over the fights and detonate them, Proper was accused of saying.

The explosions ostensibly would “force the crowd attending the … event and high value targets … to evacuate,” at which point attackers would fire on them with guns, Proper allegedly said.

“According to Proper, this attack was designed to ‘jumpstart’ a revolution in the United States,” the criminal complaint against him said.

Two Inland Empire men are among multiple suspects arrested in a thwarted plot to carry out a mass-casualty attack targeting a high-profile UFC event on the White House lawn, federal authorities said.

Bryan Omar Roa and Michael Alan Thomas, both Riverside County residents, were taken into custody and charged with conspiracy to commit murder. Federal officials say the plot was disrupted days before the event, with the FBI describing the coordinated intervention as having “stopped [the attack] cold.”

payload.title: FBI: Ryhmä suunnitteli iskua Valkoisen talon U***
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltain liittovaltion viranomaisten mukaan epäilty ryhmä suunnitteli iskua Valkoisen talon alueella järjestettyyn U***. Oikeusasiakirjojen mukaan suunnitelmaan olisi kuulunut räjähteillä varustettuja drooneja, tarkka-ampujia ja hyökkäys Valkoisen talon portille.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain liittovaltion poliisi FBI kertoo estäneensä suunnitellun iskun Valkoisessa talossa järjestettyyn U***. Tuoreeltaan julkistettujen oikeusasiakirjojen mukaan epäilty ryhmä olisi käyttänyt räjähteillä varustettuja drooneja paniikin synnyttämiseen ja ohjannut pakenevaa väkijoukkoa kohti tarkka-ampujia.

## Suunnitelma kohdistui suureen yleisötapahtumaan

Viranomaisten mukaan isku oli tarkoitus toteuttaa sunnuntaina Valkoisen talon eteläisellä nurmikentällä järjestetyn kutsuvierastapahtuman yhteydessä. Paikalla arvioidaan olleen noin 4 300 ihmistä. Lisäksi läheisellä fanialueella tapahtumaa pystyi seuraamaan noin 85 000 ihmistä.

Oikeusasiakirjojen mukaan osa suunnitelmasta koski lähirakennuksiin kohdistuvia iskuja räjähteillä lastatuilla drooneilla. Asiakirjoissa kuvataan myös väitetty toinen hyökkäysvaihe, jossa hyökkääjien oli määrä rynnätä Valkoisen talon portille.

FBI:n johtaja Kash Patel kertoi sosiaalisessa mediassa, että viranomaiset pysäyttivät väitetyn suunnitelman osana usean osavaltion operaatiota. CBS Newsin mukaan viisi ihmistä on otettu kiinni.

## Vihje lähti epäillyn lähipiiristä

Tapaus alkoi tulla viranomaisten tietoon Ohioon liittyneen epäillyn kautta. Oikeusasiakirjojen mukaan 19-vuotias Tycen Proper oli ollut yhteydessä verkossa ryhmään, jonka syyttäjät kuvaavat ilmaisseen äärimmäisen uskonnollisia ja hallituksen vastaisia näkemyksiä.

Properin äiti otti yhteyttä paikallisiin viranomaisiin 10. kesäkuuta myöhään illalla. Hän oli huolestunut poikansa suurista asehankinnoista sekä tämän verkkoviestinnästä ryhmän kanssa. Ryhmän väitettiin kuvailleen itseään entisistä sotilaista koostuvaksi ja kristillistaustaiseksi.

Asiakirjojen mukaan ryhmä puhui vallankumouksen käynnistämisestä ampumalla tapahtumaan osallistuvia niin sanottuja korkean arvon kohteita, joiksi oli tunnistettu varakkaita henkilöitä ja poliitikkoja. Väitettyjen motiivien joukossa mainittiin tyytymättömyys hallinnon korruptioon, Epstein-aineiston käsittelyyn, datakeskusten vedenkulutukseen paikallisyhteisöissä sekä muihin hallituksen toimiin.

Yksi epäilty pidätettiin Ohiossa viime viikolla. Tutkijat saivat tämän jälkeen pääsyn salattuihin viesteihin, joiden kerrotaan koskeneen myös muita väitettyjä suunnittelijoita. Epäiltyä vastaan on nostettu syytteet muun muassa salaliitosta rikoksen tekemiseksi Yhdysvaltoja vastaan sekä liittovaltion virkamiehen murhan yrityksestä.
summary_bullets: FBI:n mukaan isku Valkoisen talon U*** estettiin ennen toteutusta.
Oikeusasiakirjoissa kuvataan suunnitelma, johon olisi kuulunut drooneja, tarkka-ampujia ja hyökkäys portille.
CBS Newsin mukaan viisi ihmistä on otettu kiinni, ja yksi epäilty pidätettiin Ohiossa viime viikolla.

His mother called local authorities late in the evening on 10 June - just days before the high-profile event - because she was concerned about his large firearms purchases and what she had seen of his online communication with a group that claimed to be made up of former military members and Christian-based. The group allegedly wanted to "jumpstart" a revolution by shooting at "high-value targets" - identified as wealthy people and politicians - attending the fight, and had specifically discussed "grievances about government corruption, the handling of the Epstein files, data centers taking up all the water in communities, and other government actions", according to court documents.

By using the drones, the plotters aimed to spark panic and draw the fleeing crowd toward a sniper team, according to the court documents.. A "second wave" of attackers then allegedly was supposed to storm the White House gate. An estimated 4,300 people were present for the invite-only event on the South Lawn - and another 85,000 were able to watch at a nearby fan zone - as 14 mixed martial arts fighters competed in back-to-back fights on Sunday, The plot was discovered through Tycen Proper, a 19-year-old Ohio man, who was communicating with a group online who "expressed ultra-religious and antigovernment sentiments," federal prosecutors said in the unsealed charges.

The FBI thwarted a plot targeting Sunday's UFC event at the White House, and has taken multiple suspects into custody, according to the agency's head, Kash Patel. Part of the plan involved striking nearby buildings with explosive-laden drones, according to court documents unsealed on Tuesday. One suspect was arrested in Ohio last week, where investigators obtained access to encrypted messages involving other alleged plotters. He has been charged with conspiracy to commit an offence against the US and attempted murder of a federal officer, according to the documents. "Allegedly planned attacks were stopped cold," Patel said in a social media post on Tuesday about the "multi-state operation". Five people are in custody, CBS News, the BBC's US news partner, reported. The BBC has requested further comment from the FBI.
